The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team** represented **Harvard University** during the **2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season**. Coached by **Tommy Amaker** in his fifth season, the team made history by winning the **Ivy League** outright for the first time since 1946 and earning the program's first-ever **NCAA Tournament bid** since the modern tournament began in 1939.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of the team:

---

### **Key Facts & Achievements**
- **Record**: 26–5 (12–2 Ivy League)
- **Ivy League Finish**: **1st place** (first outright title in 66 years)
- **NCAA Tournament**: **#12 seed** in the **West Region**
  - **First Round**: Defeated **#5 seed New Mexico** (68–62) – **Harvard’s first NCAA Tournament win in program history**
  - **Second Round**: Lost to **#4 seed Wisconsin** (70–79)
- **NIT**: Declined an invitation (first time Harvard turned down the NIT in favor of the NCAA Tournament)
- **AP Poll**: Received votes but never cracked the Top 25 (highest ranking: **#25 in the Coaches Poll** post-New Mexico win)
- **KenPom Ranking**: Finished **#35** (highest in program history at the time)

---

### **Roster & Key Players**
The 2011–12 team was led by a core of experienced players, many of whom were recruited by Amaker and developed into Ivy League stars. Here are the key contributors:

#### **Starting Lineup**
1. **Keith Wright** (Sr., F/C – **6'8"**)
   - **Ivy League Player of the Year** (2011–12)
   - **First-team All-Ivy** (2010–11, 2011–12)
   - **Team leader in points (16.3 PPG) and rebounds (8.1 RPG)**
   - **Harvard’s all-time leading scorer at the time** (1,543 points)
   - Went undrafted in the 2012 NBA Draft but played professionally in Europe.

2. **Oliver McNally** (Sr., G – **6'3"**)
   - **Team captain** and floor general
   - **10.1 PPG, 3.5 APG, 42.9% 3PT**
   - Hit the **game-winning shot** in Harvard’s **67–65 win over Florida State** (Dec. 29, 2011) – one of the biggest non-conference wins in program history.
   - Played professionally in Germany after graduation.

3. **Kyle Casey** (Jr., F – **6'7"**)
   - **11.3 PPG, 5.5 RPG, 1.3 BPG**
   - **Second-team All-Ivy** (2011–12)
   - Later withdrew from Harvard in 2012 due to an academic scandal (see below) but returned for his senior year in 2013–14.

4. **Brandyn Curry** (Jr., G – **6'1"**)
   - **7.2 PPG, 4.3 APG, 1.7 SPG**
   - **Ivy League Defensive Player of the Year** (2011–12)
   - Also withdrew in 2012 due to the academic scandal but returned for 2013–14.

5. **Christian Webster** (Jr., G – **6'5"**)
   - **9.8 PPG, 40.3% 3PT**
   - **Clutch shooter**, hit big shots in key games (e.g., vs. New Mexico in the NCAA Tournament).

#### **Bench & Role Players**
- **Laurent Rivard** (So., G – **6'5"**)
  - **6.0 PPG, 40.7% 3PT** (later became a star in 2012–13)
- **Steve Moundou-Missi** (So., F – **6'7"**)
  - **3.8 PPG, 3.0 RPG** (developed into a key player in later years)
- **Jonah Travis** (Fr., F – **6'6"**)
  - **2.1 PPG, 1.8 RPG** (future starter)
- **Wes Saunders** (Fr., G – **6'5"**)
  - **1.5 PPG** (later became a two-time Ivy League Player of the Year)

---

### **Season Highlights & Key Games**
#### **Non-Conference Play (14–1 Record)**
- **Nov. 11, 2011**: **Harvard 66, MIT 53** (season opener)
- **Nov. 21, 2011**: **Harvard 69, Utah 48** (first game of the **Battle 4 Atlantis** tournament)
- **Nov. 25, 2011**: **Harvard 75, UCF 65** (Battle 4 Atlantis semifinals)
- **Nov. 26, 2011**: **Harvard 59, Florida State 53** (Battle 4 Atlantis championship – **program’s first in-season tournament title**)
  - **Keith Wright** named tournament MVP.
- **Dec. 29, 2011**: **Harvard 67, #22 Florida State 65** (Oliver McNally’s buzzer-beater)
- **Jan. 7, 2012**: **Harvard 80, Boston College 67** (first win over BC since 1995)

#### **Ivy League Play (12–2 Record)**
- **Feb. 10, 2012**: **Harvard 65, Princeton 56** (clinched at least a share of the Ivy title)
- **Mar. 3, 2012**: **Harvard 70, Cornell 69** (OT win to secure **outright Ivy League title**)
- **Mar. 6, 2012**: **Harvard 69, Yale 62** (final regular-season game – 26–4 record)

#### **NCAA Tournament**
- **Mar. 15, 2012**: **Harvard 68, #5 New Mexico 62** (Albuquerque, NM)
  - **First NCAA Tournament win in program history**
  - **Wesley Saunders** (a freshman) had a breakout game with **10 points**.
  - **Keith Wright** led with **17 points and 6 rebounds**.
- **Mar. 17, 2012**: **Harvard 70, #4 Wisconsin 79**
  - **Christian Webster** scored **18 points**, but Harvard fell short in the Round of 32.

---

### **Coaching Staff**
- **Head Coach**: **Tommy Amaker** (5th season)
  - Hired in 2007, Amaker transformed Harvard from an Ivy League doormat into a national contender.
  - Later led Harvard to **three more NCAA Tournament appearances** (2013, 2014, 2015).
- **Assistant Coaches**:
  - **Kenny Blakeney** (later became head coach at Howard)
  - **Brian DeLaney**
  - **Yanni Hufnagel** (later an assistant at Vanderbilt, Nevada, and California)

---

### **Legacy & Impact**
1. **First NCAA Tournament Win**
   - Harvard’s victory over New Mexico was the **first NCAA Tournament win by an Ivy League team since 1998** (Princeton over UCLA).
   - It marked the **beginning of Harvard’s rise as an Ivy League powerhouse**.

2. **End of Princeton’s Ivy Dominance**
   - Princeton had won or shared **13 of the previous 16 Ivy League titles** before Harvard’s 2011–12 breakthrough.

3. **Academic Scandal (2012)**
   - Just months after the season, **Kyle Casey and Brandyn Curry** were implicated in a **cheating scandal** involving a take-home exam.
   - Both withdrew from Harvard for the **2012–13 season** (Curry later returned; Casey transferred to play at **Wagner** before returning).
   - The scandal was a major setback, but Harvard still won the Ivy League in **2012–13** without them.

4. **Program Ascension**
   - The 2011–12 team laid the foundation for Harvard’s **four straight NCAA Tournament appearances (2012–2015)**.
   - Amaker’s recruiting improved, bringing in future NBA players like **Jeremy Lin (2010–12, though he left before this season)** and **Wesley Saunders**.

5. **National Recognition**
   - Harvard became a **regular in the AP Top 25 polls** in subsequent years.
   - The program’s success helped **increase applications to Harvard** and boosted its athletic reputation.

---

### **Statistical Leaders (2011–12)**
| Category       | Player            | Stat       |
|----------------|-------------------|------------|
| **Points**     | Keith Wright      | 16.3 PPG   |
| **Rebounds**   | Keith Wright      | 8.1 RPG    |
| **Assists**    | Brandyn Curry     | 4.3 APG    |
| **Steals**     | Brandyn Curry     | 1.7 SPG    |
| **Blocks**     | Kyle Casey        | 1.3 BPG    |
| **FG%**        | Keith Wright      | 54.7%      |
| **3PT%**       | Christian Webster | 40.3%      |
| **FT%**        | Oliver McNally    | 83.3%      |

---

### **Awards & Honors**
- **Keith Wright**
  - **Ivy League Player of the Year**
  - **First-team All-Ivy**
  - **NABC All-District 13 First Team**
  - **Lou Henson Award Finalist** (mid-major POY)
- **Brandyn Curry**
  - **Ivy League Defensive Player of the Year**
  - **Second-team All-Ivy**
- **Kyle Casey**
  - **Second-team All-Ivy**
- **Tommy Amaker**
  - **Ivy League Coach of the Year**

---

### **Where Are They Now?**
| Player          | Post-Harvard Career |
|-----------------|---------------------|
| **Keith Wright** | Played professionally in Europe (Germany, Italy, Israel) |
| **Oliver McNally** | Played in Germany, later became a coach (assistant at Harvard, then head coach at **Babson College**) |
| **Kyle Casey** | Played at Wagner, then professionally in Europe (Germany, Israel) |
| **Brandyn Curry** | Played professionally in Germany, later became a coach (assistant at **Harvard**) |
| **Christian Webster** | Played professionally in Germany and the G League |
| **Laurent Rivard** | Played professionally in France and the G League |
| **Wes Saunders** | Played professionally in the G League and overseas (Germany, Israel) |
| **Steve Moundou-Missi** | Played professionally in Europe (France, Germany) |

---

### **Fun Facts**
- Harvard’s **26 wins** were the most in program history at the time.
- The team’s **RPI of 35** was the highest in Ivy League history (until Yale in 2016).
- **Jeremy Lin** (Class of 2010) had already left for the NBA, but his success helped raise Harvard’s profile before the 2011–12 season.
- The **Battle 4 Atlantis championship** was Harvard’s first in-season tournament title.
- The **New Mexico win** was the first time a **#12 seed** beat a **#5 seed** in the NCAA Tournament since **2009** (Arizona over Utah).

---

### **Conclusion**
The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson** were a **historic team** that broke barriers for Ivy League basketball. Their **NCAA Tournament win over New Mexico** was a landmark moment, proving that the Ancient Eight could compete with power-conference schools. While the **academic scandal** marred the aftermath, the program’s success under **Tommy Amaker** continued, making Harvard a **national contender** in the years that followed.
